transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I’ve felt down for a long time. It’s this flat, heavy feeling most days—like even if work is going okay or people are being nice, I still feel kind of empty.
Roughly how long have you been feeling this way?
About two years and two months now. It started around the time that dashboard project put me in the spotlight at work.
Over these past two years, have there been any periods lasting more than two months where you felt completely back to your normal self?
No, I haven’t had a stretch like that. It’s been there pretty consistently for the whole two years and two months, since that dashboard project at work.
Have you ever had times where you felt unusually energized, hyper, or on top of the world, needing much less sleep than usual?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed periods where I felt unusually energized or needed a lot less sleep.
During this time, have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy?
I'm not really sure. I haven't thought about it in those terms.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels, like feeling constantly tired or fatigued?

Yeah. By the afternoon I’m usually so wiped out that even fixing a spreadsheet error or finishing expense paperwork feels like I’m dragging my body and brain through mud. Even getting myself to soccer can feel like a lot.
How has your sleep been during this time?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid close attention to my sleep.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over this time?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything specific with my appetite or weight.
How have you been feeling about yourself during this time—do you struggle with feelings of low self-esteem or feeling bad about who you are?

Yeah, I do. People still mention this dashboard I built at work, but I just feel like I somehow fooled them into thinking I’m good at my job. Then if I miss a follow-up or send an email late, it feels like proof that I’m not really as capable as they think.
